name: algebra_one_year
title: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics (one year)

metadata.course: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: A full-year integrated mathematics course: number and quantity, algebra, functions, geometry and measurement, statistics and probability.

concepts.title: Absolute value as distance
concepts.summary: Absolute value measures distance from zero and therefore discards direction while keeping size.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Absolute value equations
concepts.summary: An absolute value equation splits into two cases because two numbers sit at the same distance from zero.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Absolute value functions
concepts.summary: The absolute value function is two linear pieces joined at a vertex, which explains its V-shaped graph.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Absolute value inequalities
concepts.summary: Distance reasoning turns an absolute value inequality into a compound inequality rather than two separate cases.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Adding and subtracting polynomials
concepts.summary: Polynomials combine by matching like terms, and subtracting requires distributing the minus sign across every term.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Angle relationships
concepts.summary: Complementary, supplementary and vertical angles are fixed arithmetic relationships, not estimates.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Applications: tax, tip, discount and interest
concepts.summary: Everyday percent problems are one proportional structure wearing different words.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Arithmetic sequences as linear functions
concepts.summary: An arithmetic sequence is a linear function restricted to whole-number inputs, with the common difference as slope.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Box plots and five-number summaries
concepts.summary: A box plot displays the five-number summary, which shows centre, spread and skew in one picture.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Choosing an efficient method for quadratics
concepts.summary: Factoring, completing the square and the formula all work, and the choice is a judgement about the numbers involved.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Choosing an efficient solution method
concepts.summary: Method choice is a judgement about which form the equations are already in, not a rule about correctness.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Circumference and area of circles
concepts.summary: Circle measurements are proportional to the radius and to its square respectively, which is why pi appears in both.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Combining like terms
concepts.summary: Only terms with identical variable parts can be merged, because only they describe the same kind of quantity.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Comparing distributions
concepts.summary: Comparing two distributions requires centre, spread and shape together, because any one alone is misleading.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Comparing linear and absolute value models
concepts.summary: Choosing between a linear and an absolute value model is a claim about the shape of the underlying relationship.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Comparing linear and exponential growth
concepts.summary: Linear growth adds a constant while exponential growth multiplies by one, and the ordering of the two eventually reverses.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Composite figures and decomposition
concepts.summary: Decomposing an unfamiliar region into familiar pieces is the standard route to its area.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Compound events and the addition rule
concepts.summary: The probability of either event requires subtracting the overlap, otherwise the intersection is counted twice.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Compound inequalities
concepts.summary: An "and" compound restricts to an interval while an "or" compound allows two separate rays.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Compound interest
concepts.summary: Compound interest is exponential growth where the base is one plus the periodic rate.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Computing slope from graphs, tables and points
concepts.summary: The slope formula is a difference quotient, and the point order must be consistent in numerator and denominator.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Conditional probability
concepts.summary: Conditional probability restricts the sample space to the known condition, which changes the denominator.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Conditional relative frequency
concepts.summary: Conditioning on a row or column converts counts into rates that can be compared across groups.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Congruence and rigid motions
concepts.summary: Congruent figures are related by translations, rotations and reflections, none of which change size or shape.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Consecutive integer and age problems
concepts.summary: These problems are linear equations in disguise, and the modelling step is where they are won or lost.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Correlation and causation
concepts.summary: Two quantities moving together is evidence of association only, and association alone does not establish a cause.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Data types and variables
concepts.summary: Whether a variable is categorical or quantitative decides which summaries and displays are meaningful.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Decimals, fractions and percent equivalence
concepts.summary: Decimals, fractions and percent are three notations for the same rational quantity, and converting between them is a routine move.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Density and measurement unit conversion
concepts.summary: Density is a rate of mass per volume, so converting units converts the density too.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Dimensional analysis and unit conversion
concepts.summary: Tracking units as if they were algebraic quantities catches conversion errors before they reach an answer.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Direct variation
concepts.summary: Direct variation is a proportional relationship written as an equation through the origin.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Discrete and continuous domains
concepts.summary: A countable set of inputs gives a discrete domain while an unbroken interval gives a continuous one.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Domain and range
concepts.summary: Domain collects the permitted inputs and range the resulting outputs, and both can be restricted by context.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Equations with fractions and decimals
concepts.summary: Clearing denominators by multiplying every term by the common denominator removes fractions without changing the solution.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Equations with variables on both sides
concepts.summary: Collecting variable terms on one side and constants on the other reduces any linear equation to a two-step form.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Estimating and locating irrational numbers
concepts.summary: Irrational numbers cannot be written as a ratio of integers, so they are placed by approximation rather than exact form.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Evaluating expressions
concepts.summary: Substituting a value and computing is the direct test of what an expression means.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Evaluating functions and reading graphs
concepts.summary: Evaluating a function and reading a value off its graph are the same act performed in two representations.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Expanding products of binomials
concepts.summary: Every term of one factor multiplies every term of the other, so a two-by-two product produces four terms before simplification.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Expected value
concepts.summary: Expected value is a probability-weighted average outcome, which is what makes it a long-run prediction rather than a guarantee.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Experimental probability and the law of large numbers
concepts.summary: Experimental probability converges towards theoretical probability as the number of trials grows, which is why small samples mislead.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Exponential functions and their graphs
concepts.summary: An exponential function has a constant ratio between successive outputs, which produces its characteristic curve.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Exponential growth and decay
concepts.summary: Repeated multiplication by a constant factor produces growth or decay, which is qualitatively different from repeated addition.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Exponential modelling in context
concepts.summary: Population, depreciation and radioactive decay all share the same multiplicative structure.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Factoring out a common monomial factor
concepts.summary: Factoring begins by removing the largest shared factor, which is the distributive property run backwards.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Factoring trinomials with leading coefficient one
concepts.summary: For a monic quadratic, two numbers must meet a sum condition and a product condition simultaneously.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Factoring trinomials with leading coefficient other than one
concepts.summary: When the leading coefficient is not one, the factor pair search must also account for the leading term.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Factors, multiples and divisibility
concepts.summary: Divisibility rules let you test factor structure without dividing, which speeds up later work with fractions and polynomials.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Fraction addition and subtraction
concepts.summary: Fractions can only be combined once they name the same size of piece, so a common unit comes first.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Fraction equivalence
concepts.summary: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number renames a quantity without changing it.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Fraction multiplication and division
concepts.summary: Multiplication scales one fraction by another; division asks how many of one fraction fit inside another.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Frequency tables and dot plots
concepts.summary: Counting how often each value occurs is the first step in every summary statistic.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Function notation
concepts.summary: Function notation names the rule and the input together, which makes substitution explicit.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Functions and the vertical line test
concepts.summary: A relation is a function when each input has exactly one output, which the vertical line test detects graphically.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Geometric modelling with algebraic expressions
concepts.summary: Expressing an area or volume with a variable turns a geometry question into an algebra question.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Geometric sequences
concepts.summary: A geometric sequence is an exponential function restricted to whole-number inputs, with the common ratio as base.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Graphing inequalities on the number line
concepts.summary: An open circle excludes the boundary and a closed circle includes it, which is the visual record of strictness.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Graphing linear inequalities in two variables
concepts.summary: A two-variable inequality shades a half-plane bounded by the corresponding line.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Greatest common factor and least common multiple
concepts.summary: The GCF is the largest shared divisor and the LCM the smallest shared multiple; both come straight out of prime factorisation.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Histograms and binning
concepts.summary: A histogram groups quantitative data into bins, and the bin width changes the shape you see.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Independent and dependent variables
concepts.summary: Naming which quantity drives which is a modelling decision, and it determines which axis carries which variable.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Independent events and the multiplication rule
concepts.summary: Independent events multiply because one event does not change the other probability.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Inequality notation and solution sets
concepts.summary: An inequality describes a range of values rather than a single number, and the solution set is that whole range.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Integer addition and subtraction
concepts.summary: Adding a signed number moves along the number line; subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Integer exponents
concepts.summary: A positive integer exponent counts repeated factors, which is not the same as repeated addition.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Integer multiplication and division
concepts.summary: The sign rules for products and quotients follow from repeated addition, and they set up sign handling in algebra.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Interpreting slope and intercept in context
concepts.summary: In a model the slope and intercept carry units and meaning, and misreading either produces a plausible but wrong claim.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Interpreting slope and intercept in data context
concepts.summary: In a fitted model the slope is a predicted change per unit and the intercept a predicted baseline, both with units.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Interval notation
concepts.summary: Interval notation compresses an inequality solution set into a compact pair of endpoints.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Introduction to linear programming
concepts.summary: Optimising a linear objective under linear constraints is solved at the vertices of the feasible region.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Lines of best fit and residuals
concepts.summary: A residual is the vertical gap between an observation and the fitted line, and its pattern diagnoses whether the line fits.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Literal equations and formulas
concepts.summary: Solving a formula for a different variable uses the same operations, treating the other variables as numbers.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Logarithms as inverses of exponentials
concepts.summary: A logarithm answers what exponent produces a given value, which makes it the inverse of an exponential.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Making and critiquing data-based claims
concepts.summary: A defensible claim names the population, the sample, the method and the uncertainty, and stops short of causation without a suitable design.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Measures of centre: mean, median and mode
concepts.summary: The mean uses every value, the median uses position and the mode records the most common value, and each is affected differently by skew.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Measures of spread: range and interquartile range
concepts.summary: Range uses only the extremes while the interquartile range describes the middle half, which makes it resistant to outliers.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Mixture, rate and work problems
concepts.summary: Rates and mixtures combine as weighted sums, which produce linear equations in one unknown.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Modelling constraints with inequalities
concepts.summary: A constraint states a range the answer may occupy, which is naturally an inequality rather than an equation.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Modelling with linear equations
concepts.summary: Translating a situation into an equation requires naming the unknown and writing what the situation asserts.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Multi-step equations with distribution
concepts.summary: Removing parentheses first turns a multi-step equation into a familiar linear one.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: One-step equations
concepts.summary: A single inverse operation isolates the variable when only one operation is applied to it.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Outliers and their effect on summaries
concepts.summary: An outlier moves the mean much more than the median, so the choice of summary is a judgement about the data.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
concepts.summary: Parallel lines share a slope while perpendicular slopes multiply to negative one, both of which follow from the geometry.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Parallel lines and transversals
concepts.summary: A transversal across parallel lines creates equal and supplementary angle pairs that let you transfer information.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Parent functions and their graphs
concepts.summary: A parent function is the simplest member of a family, and every other member is a transformation of it.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Percent as a rate per hundred
concepts.summary: Percent is a ratio with an implicit denominator of one hundred, which is why it converts directly to a decimal.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Percent change
concepts.summary: Percent change compares the size of a change to the original quantity, so the base must be stated.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Perimeter and area of polygons
concepts.summary: Perimeter measures a boundary while area measures a region, and confusing the two changes the units of the answer.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Permutations and combinations
concepts.summary: Permutations count arrangements where order matters and combinations count selections where it does not.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Piecewise-defined functions
concepts.summary: A piecewise rule applies different formulas on different parts of the domain, and each piece needs its own interval.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Place value and base-ten structure
concepts.summary: Each digit carries a value set by its position, which is what makes regrouping possible.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Plotting points and identifying quadrants
concepts.summary: Quadrant location is determined by the signs of the coordinates, which makes sign errors visible immediately.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Point-slope form
concepts.summary: Point-slope form builds a line from one known point and the rate, which suits data with a natural starting observation.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Points, lines, rays and planes
concepts.summary: These undefined terms are the vocabulary every later geometric statement is built from.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Polynomial vocabulary and degree
concepts.summary: The degree is the highest exponent present and the leading coefficient governs end behaviour.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Power of a power and power of a product
concepts.summary: An outer exponent distributes over a product and multiplies against an inner exponent.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Precision, accuracy and significant figures
concepts.summary: Precision describes the fineness of a measurement while accuracy describes its closeness to the true value, and they are independent.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Prime factorisation
concepts.summary: Every whole number above one factors uniquely into primes, giving one canonical description of a number.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Probability distributions
concepts.summary: A probability distribution lists every value of a random variable with its probability, and the probabilities sum to one.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Product and quotient rules for exponents
concepts.summary: Multiplying like bases adds exponents because it concatenates two runs of identical factors.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Proportional relationships
concepts.summary: Two quantities are proportional when their ratio is constant, so scaling one scales the other by the same factor.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Quadratic expressions and their graphs
concepts.summary: A quadratic has a nonzero squared term, and its graph is a parabola whose vertex is the turning point.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Quadratic models and optimisation
concepts.summary: A quadratic models any quantity with a constant second difference, and its vertex is the maximum or minimum of that model.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Rational exponents
concepts.summary: A fractional exponent names a root, which unifies radical notation with exponent rules.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Ratios as comparisons
concepts.summary: A ratio compares two quantities of the same or different kinds, and the order of the terms carries meaning.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Reflections of graphs
concepts.summary: A negative outside the function reflects vertically while a negative inside reflects horizontally.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Relations and multiple representations
concepts.summary: The same relation can be shown as a table, a graph, a set of pairs or an equation, and each view hides different things.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Reversing the inequality symbol
concepts.summary: Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses order, which is why the symbol flips.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Sample spaces and outcomes
concepts.summary: A sample space lists every possible outcome, and the list must be exhaustive and mutually exclusive.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Sampling bias and variability
concepts.summary: A biased sample systematically misses part of the population, while variability is the unavoidable spread between samples.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Sampling methods
concepts.summary: Simple random, systematic, stratified and cluster sampling each have different practical costs and assumptions.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Scale drawings and scale factor
concepts.summary: A scale drawing preserves shape while changing size, and the scale factor connects drawing lengths to real lengths.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Scatter plots and association
concepts.summary: A scatter plot shows whether two quantitative variables are associated, and in which direction and form.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Scatter plots and lines of best fit
concepts.summary: A line of best fit summarises a linear trend, and how close the points sit to it decides how much the summary is worth.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Scientific notation
concepts.summary: Scientific notation writes a number as a mantissa times a power of ten, which makes extreme magnitudes readable and comparable.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Signed numbers on the number line
concepts.summary: A negative sign records direction relative to zero, not merely a subtraction waiting to happen.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Similar figures and scale factor
concepts.summary: Similar figures share angles and have proportional sides, which is what makes indirect measurement possible.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Simplifying linear expressions
concepts.summary: Simplifying means rewriting an expression in an equivalent but shorter form, verified by substitution.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Simplifying radical expressions
concepts.summary: A radical simplifies by pulling out the largest perfect-square factor, which is factoring under a root.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Simulation and probability models
concepts.summary: A simulation estimates a probability by generating many trials, which is useful when a theoretical model is hard to write down.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Slope as a constant rate of change
concepts.summary: Slope is the change in output per unit change in input, which is why it carries units.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Slope-intercept form
concepts.summary: Writing a line as y equals mx plus b exposes the rate and the starting value directly.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solutions and equivalent equations
concepts.summary: An equation asserts equality, and applying the same reversible operation to both sides preserves the solution set.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving one- and two-step inequalities
concepts.summary: Inequalities solve with the same inverse operations as equations, with one exception.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving proportions
concepts.summary: Cross multiplication is a shortcut that follows from multiplying both sides of an equality of ratios by the same product.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving quadratic equations by completing the square
concepts.summary: Completing the square rewrites a quadratic as a perfect square plus a constant, which exposes the vertex and the roots.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving quadratic equations by factoring
concepts.summary: Factoring converts a quadratic equation into two linear equations, each of which is easy to solve.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving simple exponential equations
concepts.summary: When both sides share a base, matching exponents solves the equation; otherwise estimation or logarithms are required.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving systems by elimination
concepts.summary: Elimination adds or subtracts multiples of equations so one variable cancels, leaving a single-variable equation.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving systems by graphing
concepts.summary: Graphing shows the solution as an intersection, which makes the meaning of no solution and infinite solutions visible.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Solving systems by substitution
concepts.summary: Substitution replaces one variable with an equivalent expression so that a two-variable problem becomes one-variable.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Special products: difference of squares and perfect squares
concepts.summary: Recognising a special product pattern lets you factor in one step instead of searching for a factor pair.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Special systems: no solution and infinitely many
concepts.summary: Parallel distinct lines share no point and coincident lines share every point, and the algebra reports both cases.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Square roots and perfect squares
concepts.summary: A square root reverses squaring, and perfect squares let you factor a root exactly.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Standard deviation
concepts.summary: Standard deviation averages squared deviations from the mean, so it describes typical distance from centre.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Standard, factored and vertex forms
concepts.summary: The three forms of a quadratic each expose a different feature: intercepts, roots, or the vertex.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Standard form and intercepts
concepts.summary: Standard form makes the x and y intercepts easy to read, which is useful for constraints written as equations.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Step functions and modelling
concepts.summary: A step function is constant on intervals, which fits any quantity that changes in discrete jumps.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Stretches and compressions
concepts.summary: A factor outside the function stretches or compresses vertically, and its reciprocal does the same horizontally.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Surface area of prisms and cylinders
concepts.summary: Surface area sums the areas of every face, and a net makes the individual faces countable.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Systems as simultaneous constraints
concepts.summary: A solution to a system must satisfy every equation at once, which is why it is an intersection rather than a root.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Systems modelling two constraints
concepts.summary: Two unknowns with two conditions produce a system, and each equation encodes one condition.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Systems with three variables
concepts.summary: Three unknowns need three independent equations, and elimination extends to that case one variable at a time.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Terms, coefficients and constants
concepts.summary: An expression is a sum of terms, and each term carries its own sign and coefficient.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The coordinate plane and ordered pairs
concepts.summary: An ordered pair records horizontal then vertical position, and the order is part of the meaning.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The correlation coefficient
concepts.summary: The correlation coefficient measures the strength and direction of a linear association only, and it is not a percentage.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The distance formula
concepts.summary: The distance formula is the Pythagorean theorem applied to a difference in coordinates.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The distributive property
concepts.summary: Multiplication distributes over addition, which is what lets you remove parentheses correctly.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The midpoint formula
concepts.summary: The midpoint formula averages coordinates, which places a point exactly halfway between two others.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The Pythagorean theorem
concepts.summary: In a right triangle the squares on the legs sum to the square on the hypotenuse, which converts between distances.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The quadratic formula and the discriminant
concepts.summary: The quadratic formula solves every quadratic, and the discriminant reports how many real roots exist before you compute them.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: The zero-product property
concepts.summary: A product equals zero only when at least one factor equals zero, which is what turns factoring into a solution method.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Theoretical probability
concepts.summary: Theoretical probability divides favourable equally likely outcomes by all equally likely outcomes.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Transforming exponential functions
concepts.summary: Shifts and stretches move an exponential curve without changing the fact that it is exponential.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Translating verbal statements into expressions
concepts.summary: Moving from words to symbols requires deciding what each quantity is before choosing operations.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Translations of graphs
concepts.summary: Adding inside the input shifts the graph horizontally in the opposite direction to the sign.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Triangle angle sum and exterior angles
concepts.summary: The interior angles of a triangle sum to a straight angle, and an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Two-step equations
concepts.summary: Undo addition before multiplication, because the order of inverse operations reverses the order of the original operations.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Two-way frequency tables
concepts.summary: A two-way table cross-classifies two categorical variables, which makes joint and marginal counts visible.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Unit rates
concepts.summary: A unit rate divides a comparison down to a single unit of the second quantity, which makes prices and speeds comparable.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Variables and algebraic notation
concepts.summary: A variable names a quantity that may vary, and juxtaposition is the conventional way to write multiplication.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Volume of prisms, cylinders and spheres
concepts.summary: Volume multiplies a base area by a height, with the sphere formula as the notable exception.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Writing equations of lines from context
concepts.summary: Turning a described situation into a line requires identifying the rate and one known point.

provenance.source: Algebra I and Integrated Mathematics — one year

concepts.title: Zero and negative exponents
concepts.summary: The rules extend to zero and negative exponents in exactly the way that keeps the quotient rule consistent.
